document.title: Afghanistan: GOP denies Pakistani Involvement in Fighting; Taliban Reportedly Enlisting Supporters in Frontier Areas
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Confidential] A US officer talks with Pakistani Afghan desk officer Naeem Khan and Taliban Embassy First Secretary Abdul Wahab. Khan denies military aid, admitting only diplomatic support. Wahab denies official Pakistani support but admits manpower from Pakistan's NWFP tribal areas.

events.description: Poloff meets Naeem Khan of Pakistani MFA, who denies Pakistani military involvement.
Poloff meets Abdul Wahab, who denies Pakistani assistance and direct Taliban recruitment.
Latest round of fighting begins in mid-May; Taliban suffer defeats in the north.
Traffic jam of trucks and buses taking young men from Haripur camp to Afghanistan; large crowd at Kandahar airport.
US Embassy Islamabad cable reporting on Taliban recruitment and Pakistani denials.
Poloff meets Naeem Khan; Khan denies Pakistani military involvement in Afghanistan fighting.
Poloff meets Abdul Wahab, who denies Pakistani aid and direct Taliban recruitment.
Latest round of fighting in northern Afghanistan began in mid-May; Taliban suffered defeats.
Traffic jam at Haripur as trucks and buses carried young men to Afghanistan; over 5,000 reportedly crossed.
Large crowd of Taliban supporters seen at Kandahar airport.
Cable sent by US Embassy Islamabad reporting GOP denials and Taliban recruitment.

key_claims: Pakistan's MFA denied that Pakistani military forces fight in Afghanistan, admitting only diplomatic support to the Taliban.
The Taliban embassy denied Pakistani assistance and denied direct recruitment, while acknowledging volunteers from frontier areas.
Observers said the Taliban were recruiting from frontier tribes, madrassahs and refugee camps after northern battlefield defeats.
Madrassahs in NWFP and Balochistan were reportedly emptied as Afghan students left to fight, after a call by Mullah Omar.
Refugee estimates suggested over 5,000 men recently crossed into Afghanistan from Pakistan.
The US Embassy doubted Pakistani military units were fighting, and thought the new recruits lacked military training.
